entries.title: Intuit agrees to sell marketing subsidiary Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68B in cash and stock; Intuit paid $12B to buy Mailchimp in 2021 (Jordan Novet/CNBC)
At a Senate hearing, Trump's CISA director nominee Michael LoSapio dodged questions about the agency's priorities, denied January 6 was an attack, and more (Eric Geller/Cybersecurity Dive)
Source: Meta plans to charge $300 for its forthcoming Muse Charm device and include a free 5G data plan from Verizon for up to 12 months (Jyoti Mann/The Information)
A bipartisan group of 24+ House lawmakers forms the AI Safety and Innovation Caucus, seeking to balance mitigating AI risks with maintaining US leadership in AI (Owen Dahlkamp/Politico)
Google adds computer use to Gemini for macOS, letting it work across apps, files, and the web in the background, available to US AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra users (Sarah Perez/TechCrunch)
Everful, which connects smaller retailers and brands with Chinese factories and manages the process from order to delivery, raised a $48.5M Series A (Kate Park/TechCrunch)
Kalshi partners with smaller rival Novig to ask 35 states for access to "self-exclusion lists", which identify gambling addicts, to restrict problem gamblers (Bobby Allyn/Bloomberg)
Ubisoft reports Q2 net bookings down 21% YoY to €388.9M, above €350.7M est., driven by Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, as it overhauls its operations (Mauro Orru/Wall Street Journal)
Google built a "Mirror Dimension", an isolated internet with simulated environments like social media and banking dashboards, to test AI browsing agents (Lily Hay Newman/Wired)
Sources: Alphabet plans to raise at least CA$5B in a five-part Canadian bond sale, after raising CA$8.5B in its debut Canadian offering in May (Bloomberg)
London-based Boltz, which is developing AI models to speed up drug discovery, raised a $110M Series A led by Bessemer, after raising a $28M seed in 2025 (John Reynolds/Tech.eu)
Anthropic closes up 17% at $97.17 in its Nasdaq debut, giving it a market cap of $1.3T, after opening at $111.50, up 34% from its IPO price (Reuters)
Anthropic opens at $111.50 per share in record IPO: Live updates (CNBC)
AMD's shares fall 6%+ after Hunterbrook disclosed a short position, warning AMD is engaging in "circular deals" and "has made way more promises" than Nvidia (Lynn Doan/Bloomberg)
Amazon warns NYC customers that they could be charged up to $5 more per order if the City Council passes a bill requiring it to directly hire delivery workers (Lisa Fickenscher/New York Post)
